newsitem.title: UK: Novorossiisk crude exports delayed 5-6 days - trade.
newsitem.headline: Novorossiisk crude exports delayed 5-6 days - trade.

text.p: Crude loadings at Russia's main oil export port of Novorossiisk on the Black Sea have been delayed for five or six days and gas oil exports have also diminished recently, oil traders said on Tuesday.
A shipping inspector said the delays were due to three scheduled crude pipeline shutdowns in September, but traders said it could also be related to bad weather delays at the end of August.
"All the programme has been pushed back by five or six days...Transneft has issued a new schedule," a major buyer of Russian crude said on Tuesday.
The shipping inspector said the smaller 20,000 tonnes per day crude pipeline feeding the port was shut for repairs, leaving only the 90,000 tonnes per day line open on Tuesday.

Gas oil traders said Novorossiisk gas oil loadings had diminished by about 20-30 percent recently, although no details were available. Most Russian gas oil exports come from the other Black Sea ports of Odessa and Tuapse which were both operating normally, the shipping inspector said.

It was unclear whether Novorossiisk fuel oil exports were disturbed, dealers said. One said there had been a slight reduction in loadings in the last few days, but there was no evidence that this was more than a temporary blip.
